data.title: AUDUSD is the biggest mover of the major currencies this week.  The price falls -2.30% for the week.
data.description:
The AUDUSD is the weakest of the major currencies vs the greenback. It fell -2.3%.  The price has now fallen for 10 consecutive days. That move has taken the price from a high on November 10 at 0.69296 to the low today at 0.6609 or -320 pips.  

The 320-pip slide in AUDUSD started with a repricing of Fed rate expectations and picked up steam as Australia’s jobs market weakened and the global equity selloff deepened. The Aussie’s 2.30% decline this week, the largest of the seven majors you tracked against the USD, also reflected weakness against other currencies, including the yen and euro.

data.title: Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran as military warns of strain. FT
data.description:
President Donald Trump is considering new strikes on Iran, the Financial Times reports, as hawkish officials in Washington and Israel urge him to resume military action.

U.S. military planners are warning that American forces risk becoming overextended if the standoff drags into the new year. The warning adds pressure on Trump as he weighs whether to restart strikes and how long U.S. forces can sustain their current posture.

data.title: Fed’s Cook says monetary policy isn’t restrictive enough
data.description:
The Fed’s Cook weighed in on inflation, the labor market and the need for tighter monetary policy in remarks that crossed the wires.

  • Fed’s current monetary policy stance is not providing needed restraint.
  • September’s interest rate hike was not enough to curtail high inflation.
  • High inflation does not give U.S. central bank space to be patient.
  • Holding off on rate hikes increases risk that inflation will embed in economy.
  • Data since September points to need for tighter monetary policy.
  • Current level of inflation is of “great concern.”
  • U.S. economic growth is strong, labor market is healthy and stable.
  • Embedded inflation will require more aggressive Fed response.
  • Financial conditions are too accommodative right now.
  • Tariff impact on inflation has faded.
  • Little evidence AI is weighing on job market so far.

data.title: NASDAQ composite is now down on the year
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite has given back its gains for 2026. With the index down 3.21% on the day at 23,111.52, it is now 130.47 points below its 2025 closing level of 23,241.99. That puts the index down 0.56% for the year and gives buyers a clear level to get back above if they are to start to wrestle back some control.

The Nasdaq 100 is taking the biggest hit of the five major indices, down 3.56% on the day at 25,573.95. It is still up 1.28% for 2026, but the cushion over last year’s close has narrowed to 324.10 points. That leaves the Nasdaq 100 a little more than 1% away from joining the Composite in negative territory for the year.

data.title: Could Jensen Huang end up at SpaceX? Dan Ives thinks he could work alongside Elon Musk
data.description:
SpaceX has already lined up about $40 billion in financing for AI computing equipment, including next-generation Nvidia chips.

In a Bloomberg interview about 30 minutes ago, tech analyst Dan Ives was asked where Jensen Huang might be a year from now. His answer was SpaceX. Ives floated the possibility that the Nvidia co-founder could become co-CEO alongside Elon Musk, framing it as his personal prediction.

data.title: S&P 500 turns positive, but the Nasdaq indices remain in technical triage
data.description:
The broader U.S. stock indices opened lower and are trying to find their footing after the sharp declines seen recently. The S&P 500 has been the first of the three to move back into modest positive territory. The Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq 100 have bounced off their lows but are still down on the day.

There is a difference between bouncing off a low and taking back control. For the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite, the first job is to get back above the support areas that gave way. For the Nasdaq 100, the immediate question is whether buyers can hold the retracement level tested at today’s low.

data.title: Bitcoin tests key swing area low. A break below will target the 2026 lows
data.description:
Bitcoin moved to its lowest level since early July, trading down to $61,160. That took the price $23 below the $61,183 level that marks the bottom of a key swing area on the four-hour chart, but momentum faded and the price has bounced modestly.  The buyers are trying to hold onto some control. .

The move lower extends the decline from the November 4 swing high to about $20,000, or 24.6%. From the September 21 high at $87,374, the price is down 30%. The sellers have been in control, and they are now getting another chance to push the price through support that has held since early July.

data.title: The stock market's wealth effect: why it matters even if you don't own stocks
data.description:
Equity market movements can have a significant impact on the economy through the so-called "wealth effect", changes in financial conditions and the influence on corporate investment and hiring decisions.

People can be affected by a stock market rally or selloff, even if they don't own stocks. Companies rely on financial markets to raise capital, finance expansions, make acquisitions and attract investment. When equity markets rise or collapse, the consequences can eventually reach workers, consumers and businesses across the economy.
